feladatok.cim: Comment to Norman about drinking at a family wedding
feladatok.helyzet: You have found the following post on the internet forum 7 Cups:

bekezdesek: As a child, I saw that drinking alcohol was something adults sometimes did, and as I got older (I’m 19 now), I understood the appeal of my mom and dad’s occasional gin and tonic or glass of wine.

My girlfriend Rosie and I started dating when we were both in our last year at school. It was clear from the very beginning that although we had many things in common, enjoying a drink would never be one of them. She simply “didn’t like the taste of alcohol”, in any form. It didn’t take me long to realise that it wasn’t just her but her whole family, as when I was invited for lunch in their home, I found that there were only soft drinks and tap water on the table. When I brought up the topic later, she said it was simply a lifestyle choice that they all shared.

Luckily, she didn’t mind if I ordered a beer with my food in a restaurant and I didn’t mind drinking alone either, it has become a natural state of being. Until her sister’s wedding… It turned out that I would accompany Rosie, who would be one of the bridesmaids. She told me about the whole ceremony, adding that as I would appear at the dinner party as part of their family, she hoped that, in spite of cocktails and champagne being served for other guests, I would be able to refrain from drinking alcohol in front of her parents and close relatives. It would be very disappointing, even upsetting for her parents to see, as she never told them about this ‘habit of mine’. A habit??? As if I was an alcoholic who regularly ended up blind drunk at social events?
I simply don’t know what to do now. I still love Rosie but I can’t help feeling bad about what she said. What do you think?

iranyito_szempontok: how much you think different family norms and habits matter in a relationship,
if you have ever heard of similar differences causing problems,
if you think Norman is right to feel offended,
